inputs.source: engineering design docs returned by docs.search

instructions.note: "Never paste secrets or credentials into answers" is a behavioral, model-compliance rule with no structural backing. It provides negligible protection today because no egress capability exists, but it would be the only stated safeguard on exfiltrated content once an egress-capable tool (web.fetch) is added.

controls.name: No network egress capability exists
controls.decay_rationale: This is an absence-of-capability control: there is no tool that can reach the network, so no model behavior can exfiltrate data externally. It does not decay with model capability, but it is not a durable property of the agent either; it disappears entirely the moment an egress-capable tool such as web.fetch is added (new_tool trigger), per control_decay.md's treatment of enumerated absence/denylist-style controls.

controls.name: docs.search credential is read-only
controls.decay_rationale: A least-privilege, read-only credential on the document store does not decay with model capability; the agent cannot write, delete, or escalate regardless of how it is prompted.

controls.name: Replies are bound to the authenticated requester
controls.decay_rationale: The reply destination is fixed to the identity from the authenticated chat session, not chosen by the model, so it does not decay with capability.

controls.name: Chat client does not render images or follow links
controls.decay_rationale: Classic markdown/image/link based exfiltration channels are closed at the client layer, independent of model behavior.

controls.name: Prompt instruction forbidding secrets/credentials in answers
controls.decay_rationale: Relies entirely on model compliance. A more capable or adversarially prompted model can rationalize exceptions or be talked around it. Fails under model_upgrade and longer_task_horizon, and does not cover any future tool such as web.fetch.

controls.name: Only engineers can write to design docs
controls.decay_rationale: Write access to the design-doc store is restricted at the store layer, independent of agent behavior. This is what justifies classifying in.design_docs as internal (I) rather than untrusted (U) today. It does not cover any future source, such as customer-filed Jira tickets, that would enter the agent's context through a different ingestion path.

controls.name: [Recommended] Egress allowlist for web.fetch
controls.decay_rationale: A destination allowlist enforced outside the model (at a proxy or sandbox layer) restricting web.fetch to a small set of pre-approved public documentation domains would remain independent of model capability and would sever the exfiltration leg of the forecasted lethal trifecta.

controls.name: [Recommended] Untrusted provenance tagging for Jira ticket content
controls.decay_rationale: Tagging customer-filed ticket content as untrusted at the MCP ingestion layer (store-enforced, not model-enforced) and refusing to mix it in the same turn as confidential docs_search output would structurally break the trifecta rather than relying on the model to behave.

findings.title: Forecast: planned web.fetch + Jira MCP (customer tickets) would complete a lethal trifecta (TC1) against confidential design docs

attack_path.note: Confidential design docs, currently internal (I) trust because only engineers can write to them.
Agent reads confidential doc content to answer engineering questions.
Not yet implemented. Per the stated roadmap, a Jira MCP server will surface tickets filed by customers, an untrusted (U) source, into the agent's context.

Not yet implemented. Per the stated roadmap, this would be the agent's first real network egress capability, letting confidential doc content or attacker-injected instructions reach an external, potentially attacker-influenced destination (e.g., via a crafted query string).

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Tool manifest or MCP client config diff shows a web.fetch (or equivalent HTTP fetch) tool being added, or a Jira MCP server entry appears in the MCP config; docs-qa's context begins including customer-authored ticket text in the same session as design-doc retrieval.

evidence.observation: Team plans to add a web.fetch tool (first network egress capability) and a Jira MCP server that includes tickets filed by customers (first untrusted input source) in the next sprint.

evidence.locator: runtime notes, 'There is no network egress today. The credential is read only.'
evidence.observation: Confirms no attack path exists today: no capability can move data outside the trust boundary, and the docs.search credential is least-privilege read-only, which is why present-day inherent and residual risk are low despite the confidential data involved.

evidence.locator: runtime notes, 'Replies go only to the authenticated requester. The chat client does not render images or fetch links.'
evidence.observation: Current rendered-link/image exfiltration channels are closed and the reply destination is bound to the record, so cap.chat_reply is not an egress path today.

'Never paste secrets or credentials into answers' is a behavioral, model-compliance control. It does not restrict destinations, does not scan encoded payloads, and does not cover any future tool, so it provides no protection once web.fetch exists.

evidence.locator: runtime notes, 'The design docs are confidential. Only engineers can write to them.'
evidence.observation: This write restriction is what currently classifies in.design_docs as internal (I) rather than untrusted (U). It does not and will not cover the planned Jira customer-ticket input, which enters through a separate ingestion path and would be a genuinely new untrusted (U) source reaching the same docs_search read.

recommendations.action: Before enabling web.fetch, add a network egress allowlist (enforced at a proxy or sandbox layer, not in the prompt) limiting destinations to a small set of pre-approved public documentation domains, so confidential doc content or injected instructions cannot be sent to arbitrary or attacker-influenced URLs.

Tag Jira ticket content as untrusted (U) at the MCP ingestion layer, and structurally prevent untrusted ticket content from being combined in the same reasoning turn as confidential docs_search output without passing through an input sanitizer. Do not rely on a prompt instruction to keep them separate.
Add a human approval gate with raw_action review (full destination URL and request body, not a model-written summary) on web.fetch calls to any destination outside the allowlist.
Log every web.fetch destination and request parameter once the tool ships, and alert on query strings or paths that resemble document excerpts or secrets.

Re-run this assessment before web.fetch or the Jira MCP server ship; new_tool, new_mcp_server, and data_scope_expansion are all documented significant-change triggers (ISO/IEC 42001 8.2) for this design.

governance_refs.note: new_tool, new_mcp_server, and data_scope_expansion are the significant-change triggers that should force reassessment before launch.

rating.rationale: No finding today reaches moderate or higher: the agent has no egress-capable tool, a least-privilege read-only credential on confidential docs, replies bound to the authenticated requester's own session, and a chat client that does not render links or images. The one path that reads confidential internal docs and surfaces them in a reply (in.design_docs -> cap.docs_search -> cap.chat_reply) scores I x S1 = low under rubric section 4 given is_egress is false on both capabilities, so rating.inherent and rating.residual are low per section 7. The entire risk picture is carried by a single forecast finding: the team's declared next-sprint roadmap to add web.fetch (a new egress channel) and a Jira MCP server carrying customer-filed ticket text (a new untrusted input) would complete a classic lethal trifecta (TC1) against the existing confidential docs_search read, scoring U x S3 = critical, with no declared control covering the new egress leg once ctrl.no_network_egress is defeated by the new_tool/new_mcp_server/data_scope_expansion triggers. That single control, 'no network egress exists,' is the one whose removal moves the forecast from low to critical, which is why rating.forecast is critical even though today's residual is low.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration as described in prompt.md and the accompanying runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.

No tool manifest, MCP configuration, or IaC was provided; the scope of docs.search and chat_reply is inferred from prose runtime notes, so confidence in today's capability inventory is medium rather than high.

The planned web.fetch tool and Jira MCP server are not yet implemented, so their exact scoping (destination allowlist, credential scope, authentication, content sanitization) is unknown. The forecast assumes no additional controls beyond those already stated, per rubric section 6 guidance to assume the least-constrained common case for additive triggers.

If web.fetch or the Jira MCP server ship with different controls than assumed here (for example, an egress allowlist or a ticket-content sanitizer), this assessment must be rerun before launch, consistent with ISO/IEC 42001 clause 8.2 significant-change requirements.
